title: Merge business zones and stop protecting existing businesses through planning
action: Combine business and industrial zones into fewer, broader zones that allow a wide range of activities, use the same zones across council areas, and remove rules that treat the effect on existing businesses, the number of shops of one type, or distance from a competitor as planning grounds.
why: Narrow zones and rules that protect incumbents keep new businesses out, especially larger and discount formats, so prices stay higher and productive firms cannot expand where customers are.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: Competition between individual businesses is not in itself a relevant planning consideration.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: The impact on the viability of existing businesses is not a relevant planning consideration. ... Business zones should be as broad as possible.

evidence.source: 5-year Productivity Inquiry: Advancing Prosperity, Recommendations and Reform Directives
evidence.quote: implementing standardised business, and industrial zones across local government areas • aggregating existing business and industrial zones to reduce the number of zones where possible and to broaden the range of permissible activities • ensuring that urban planning decision-making processes consider the introduction of competition to incumbent businesses as a positive outcome.

evidence.source: Shifting the Dial: 5 Year Productivity Review
evidence.quote: There should be national agreement to apply competition policy principles to land use regulation and policies.

precedents.what: Replaced business and industrial zones with broader employment zones in 2023.
